analyst_view.overall: Leaders Arsenal (28 points) host third-placed Manchester City (22) in the big game of the weekend. Arsenal drew 2-2 with Newcastle and 1-1 with Dortmund, throwing away leads in both; against Dortmund they had 30 shots but only four on target. Bukayo Saka (thigh, out since 21 October) and Martin Zubimendi (hamstring) are out, and goalkeeper David Raya is uncertain after a shoulder knock, with Kepa as cover; the numbers have no missing players for this game. City, under Enzo Maresca, have won one of their last six games, are ten games without a clean sheet and drew 2-2 with Napoli on Tuesday; Antoine Semenyo (knee) is their main absentee. No referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals: 1.6 for Arsenal and 1.0 for City. They have no missing players for this game, so they do not know Arsenal are without Saka, their main creator, and Zubimendi, or that City are without Semenyo. Arsenal have also been wasteful lately and big title games tend to be tight, so I take about 5% off, to about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.0 corners, about even, already counting City's high corner count lately. Arsenal pile on pressure and win corners even without Saka, and City's open play gives up chances in wide areas. Nothing points clearly either way, so I stay at about 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.7 cards, already counting Arsenal's rising card count and past meetings. This is a top-of-the-table clash with a lot at stake, and City have been losing duels and struggling with counter-attacks, which tends to bring tactical fouls. No referee is named yet, so I only add about 4%, to about 3.8.

shots.text: The numbers expect 24.4 shots, about even, and already count City allowing more shots than usual lately. Arsenal still take plenty of shots without Saka (30 against Dortmund), while City's high-possession style should limit them somewhat. I stay at about 24.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 7.8 shots on target. Arsenal have been taking many low-quality shots lately (4 of 30 on target against Dortmund), and without Saka and Zubimendi they lack the players who create clean chances, which the numbers do not know about. I take about 4% off, to about 7.5.
